Blood Vial is genuinely cool. I like it, and it's worth its price. I can't honestly recommend it though. There's not enough content, and I think the gameplay is kind of just above average. If it receives content updates and at least one major rework, it could 100% be an amazing game worth even more than its current price. Buy it to support indie developers. The gameplay loop, as of writing, is fighting the same few enemy types in the same very few levels. I think the levels are randomly generated, which is pretty cool, but each "cell" is very distinct and you learn them very quickly. The movement system of swimming through blood is cool, but I just don't think it adds much of value as it stands. You only need it for two things: sliding through grates and regaining health. The enemies don't force you to learn the deeper mechanics of the movement system at all, and there's just not much to play with. You only have three weapons, which don't affect much of how the game actually plays out. You'll be forced close range 90% of the entire game, so you really don't need to think about your weapon at all. The enemy types of the first 2 Acts are really lame. Act 3 steps it up a ton. There's too many "walk straight towards you" enemies and the hunter who you just have to slightly move around to avoid. There's not really any "flexing"? The game, as far as I can tell, only rewards headshots and doesn't give bonus style points for anything else right now. If you ask me there's really no need for a style system at all as it currently stands. The roguelite element is quite shallow right now. There's 3 items I actually want in any given run. The headshot ricochet item, the headshot refund item, and double jumps. Practically everything else is a stat modifier, except for wall ricochet which is practically useless in my experience. Strictly as a 5$ micro-FPS? This game is great for a few runs. But don't expect an infinitely replayable experience as the game stands right now.

This game's borderline on whether or not I'd recommend it, but I think it's ultimately worth it as long as you know what you're getting. It's extremely short, I beat the game in less than two hours of play, there's basically no challenge once you're used to the game. The gameplay is very one-note so it dries up quickly. At $5, there're other games you could spend that amount on and get much more content. What's here is fun, but there's limited replay value, I've probably finished it at least 8 times, and even then, I've only put four hours in and I'm struggling to find a reason to pick it up again. FPS Games I've paid $5 or less for and enjoyed longer than Blood Vial in no particular order: Murder Miners $2.99 Carnal $0.99 Rogue Shooter $4.99 Doom 64 $4.99 Wolfenstein 3D $4.99 Return to Castle Wolfenstein $4.99 Half Life Opposing Force $4.99 Blood and Bacon $0.99 Nosferatu: The Wrath of Malachi $2.99 Neon Shadow $4.99 Dead Effect $4.99
